audience: middle-school students learning rates and unit rates

directions_explored.name: Market Receipt Lab
directions_explored.rationale: A tactile grocery-receipt and shelf-label language makes best-buy math feel real without turning the workspace into a decorative game.

directions_explored.name: Bauhaus Math Counter
directions_explored.rationale: Bold geometry would reinforce mathematical structure, but its primary-color energy could compete with the student work.

directions_explored.name: Graph Paper Workshop
directions_explored.rationale: Familiar classroom materials feel approachable, but risk looking like a worksheet instead of an interactive simulator.

narrative_brief.visual_thesis: A warm, ink-on-paper market lab where the math feels tangible and every visual cue supports comparison.
narrative_brief.content_plan: A compact header switches Learn, Practice, and Challenge; controls select an aisle; the main workspace pairs the shopping problem with a four-step solving path; completion explains the savings.
narrative_brief.interaction_thesis: The title enters once, step panels slide when understanding advances, and the final result settles into view as a meaningful success state.
